title: The six consumed event types of the ledger intake are not stated for rwb-source-data, and the target names of the document and timer facts are not given for the intake
source: 04 User stories, Epic 1 Story Files v7, RWB E1 067 rows Preconditions, Flow, Contract and Solution plan (the six events and the event-to-entry map); 22 Microservice Realignment, Architecture v5 Text Extract v1, slides 11, 15, 41, 42 and 43 (event catalogue and the P1 service contract); _work/msr/plan/ownership.json rows processed_event, idempotency_key and interaction; Template and Rules v1 §R3 and §R7.3
section: 3 Preconditions; 4 Flow; 8 Business rules; 12.4 Events consumed; 12.7 Tables owned
description: The legacy listener names its six inputs by the monolith's event numbers: EV-01 CaseCreated, EV-02 CaseAllocated, EV-04 CaseTransferred, EV-19 TimerBreached, EV-16 DocumentStored and EV-08 DecisionRecorded. The target catalogue gives a name and a topic for each fact, but it names the consumers of every event and rwb-source-data is not among them for any of the six: rwb-source-data appears in the catalogue as a producer of AceDataReady and AceDataLate only, and Architecture v5 slide 15 gives the service no consumed event at all. The two facts whose target name matters most for the intake are the document fact (legacy EV-16 DocumentStored) and the timer fact (legacy EV-19 TimerBreached): the catalogue carries DocumentStored on the rwb-document topic and TimerBreached on the rwb-case topic, but nothing states that the ledger intake consumes either of them, and the legacy names are not the target CloudEvents types. The row also records that the hit-count table changed owner: the legacy story created processed_event in its own Flyway migration, while the Ownership Map makes processed_event and idempotency_key PLT library objects created in each service's schema under DP-09.
evidence: RWB E1 067 §3 'The publishing stories exist for EV-01 CaseCreated and EV-02 CaseAllocated (RWB-E1-018, RWB-E1-020), EV-04 CaseTransferred (RWB-E1-021), EV-16 DocumentStored (RWB-E1-024), EV-08 DecisionRecorded (RWB-E1-027) and EV-19 TimerBreached'; §13 'Database: table processed_event (new, Flyway migration in this story)'; Architecture v5 slide 42 rows 01, 02, 04, 08, 16 and 19 with the Consumer column naming rwb-agent, rwb-case, rwb-deviation, rwb-reporting, rwb-decision and gateway-bff and never rwb-source-data; slide 43 row 26-27 rwb-source-data as a producer only; slide 15 rwb-source-data IN 'events (none: Airflow call; fallback polls ACE batch record)'; _work/msr/plan/ownership.json processed_event basis 'Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 11 (inbox table processed_event in each consumer) and slide 20; plan DP-09 (RWB-PLT-TE006-CON)'
proposed: Keep the six facts of the legacy listener and read them as the six rows of the map: rwb.case.CaseCreated.v1, rwb.case.CaseAllocated.v1, rwb.case.CaseTransferred.v1 and rwb.case.TimerBreached.v1 on rwb.case.events.v1, rwb.document.DocumentStored.v1 on rwb.document.events.v1 and rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1 on rwb.decision-record.v1, with EV-16 DocumentStored read as the rwb-document fact and EV-19 TimerBreached as the rwb-case fact. Add rwb-source-data to the Consumer column of those six rows in the next version of the event catalogue, and confirm the two derived names with the rwb-document and rwb-case owners at the wave 1 entry check. Take the hit count from the PLT inbox object and drop the legacy migration from the story.

title: The format of the ledger intake map document and the exact target names of the document and timer facts are not given by any source
source: 04 User stories, Epic 1 Story Files v7, RWB E1 067 rows Contract and Solution plan (listener table and build steps); 22 Microservice Realignment, Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 42 and 43 (event catalogue); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench API Specification v4.yaml schema Interaction; _work/msr/plan/ownership.json rows interaction and processed_event; Template and Rules v1 §R7.2 and §R9
section: 10 Authority; 11 Data; 12.4 Events consumed; 13 Solution plan; 19 Out of scope
description: The legacy story gives the listener as a table of items rather than a document, and its event-to-entry map as a configuration key with six values. No source states what artefact the target intake contract is (an AsyncAPI document, a YAML map beside the OpenAPI file, or a table inside the service API file), what its version label is, or where it is published, so the baseline of RWB-P1-E1067-CON fixes the row content and leaves the file format to the review. The same hold applies to the two facts that are hardest to name: the legacy story knows EV-16 DocumentStored and EV-19 TimerBreached, and the Architecture v5 catalogue carries DocumentStored on rwb.document.events.v1 and TimerBreached on rwb.case.events.v1, but no source states that these are the two types the ledger intake consumes, or that the intake reads them as rwb.document.DocumentStored.v1 and rwb.case.TimerBreached.v1. The field names of the entry the intake sets are available (the Interaction schema of the API Specification v4), and the map format is not.
evidence: RWB E1 067 §12 table Listener rows Trigger, Input, Output, Idempotency key and Restart behavior with no document artefact; §13 build step 2 LedgerEventMapper with the configured map; Architecture v5 slide 42 rows 16 and 19 with the Consumer column naming rwb-agent, rwb-case and gateway-bff and never rwb-source-data; slide 11 Event contract row AsyncAPI 3.0 per topic, JSON Schema registry, backward compatible; API Specification v4 Interaction schema properties eventCode, actorType, actorRef, sourceRef, idempotencyKey, caseSeq, decisionLogId and correctsEntryId
proposed: Publish the intake baseline as a versioned YAML map beside the service contract files, with one row per consumed event type and the nine row fields of section 11, and validate it in the pipeline. Keep the six legacy event IDs as row labels beside the target types so the legacy criteria and the target map can be read together, and confirm the two derived type names with the rwb-document and rwb-case event owners at the wave 1 entry check. Move the file format to the service contract standard in the next version of the API and AsyncAPI guidance.
